question: Should OpenClaw add a model-facing parent-only sub-agent send contract, and should that contract be a dedicated sessions_send_parent tool or a reserved sessionKey:"parent" selector?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this changes child-to-parent session authorization and model-facing tool semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape.

options.title: Add dedicated parent-only contract
options.body: Implement a dedicated tool or trusted parent selector that derives the direct parent from active spawn metadata and rejects missing, stale, sibling, ancestor, cross-agent, and auto-forwarded targets.

options.title: Reserve parent selector
options.body: Keep one sessions_send tool but make parent a trusted selector rather than a literal user-supplied key, with the same security checks.

options.title: Decline native mid-run sends
options.body: Keep child-originated mid-run sends unsupported and document completion handoff, sessions_yield, and explicit operator opt-ins as the supported paths.

recommendation.title: Add dedicated parent-only contract
recommendation.body: Implement a dedicated tool or trusted parent selector that derives the direct parent from active spawn metadata and rejects missing, stale, sibling, ancestor, cross-agent, and auto-forwarded targets.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is most directly connected to recent sessions_send, session resolution, and sub-agent security-boundary history for the requested API.
